results: 1. adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
2. pupil size and light reaction: pupils EQUALLY REACTIVE - pupil-sparing
3. MRI brain with DWI: small DORSAL PARAMEDIAN MIDBRAIN INFARCT on diffusion-weighted imaging
4. diffusion tensor tractography: reduced integrity of the IPSILATERAL medial longitudinal fasciculus
5. CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): no aneurysm
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: WEBINO (Wall-Eyed Bilateral Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia) syndrome from an acute dorsal paramedian midbrain infarction (paramedian basilar perforator territory ischaemic stroke)
ALTERNATIVE 1: Bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia from a demyelinating lesion (e.g., multiple sclerosis) of the dorsal midbrain
ALTERNATIVE 2: One-and-a-half syndrome from a rostral pontine / ponto-mesencephalic lesion extending into the MLF
ALTERNATIVE 3: Wernicke encephalopathy (thiamine deficiency) involving the periaqueductal grey and MLF
dx: WEBINO (Wall-Eyed Bilateral Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia) syndrome from an acute dorsal paramedian midbrain infarction (paramedian basilar perforator territory ischaemic stroke)
